query:
Who expressed the view that the value of a photography session lies in intentionality rather than the number of exposures made?

Options:
A. Priya
B. Callum
C. Yuki
D. Sol
context:
[1] (about=Yuki, episodic, t0 @2025-02-01T10:26:00) My read on this is that the value of a session is rarely in the roll count. One considered frame outweighs twenty automatic ones. The pinhole exposure duration suggests that understanding regardless of format.
[2] (about=Otto, episodic, t8 @2025-03-01T10:26:00) In my experience, figural work forces a different kind of commitment from the photographer. You cannot correct for it in the darkroom the way you can correct for light. Priya's prints show that understanding.
[3] (about=Yuki, episodic, t8 @2025-03-01T10:08:00) My read on this is that the decision was Margot's indirectly. The restraint in her market roll showed me that colour could serve the image without dominating it. I shot two rolls. These are the only frames I kept.
[4] (about=Otto, episodic, t4 @2025-02-15T10:07:00) I looked at Sol's contact sheets before the session. In my experience, work that requires significant contextualisation before the viewer can engage with it is asking the context to do the work the image should do. I raise this in the spirit of critique rather than criticism.
[5] (about=Yuki, episodic, t6 @2025-02-22T10:22:00) I looked at Margot's prints before the session. The palette has a restraint I had not expected from colour work. Each frame is held together by a single dominant tone. My read on this is that the film choice was deliberate.
[6] (about=Margot, episodic, t0 @2025-02-01T10:16:00) I shot six frames on the coast during the break. Very Cartier-Bresson in the light, though not intentionally.
[7] (about=Bex, episodic, t0 @2025-02-01T10:22:00) okay but please don't make me sound talented when I barely knew what I was doing 😂 speaking of, I found this series by a Japanese photographer doing double exposure street work that is so relevant to what Sol's been trying. should I drop the link in here??
[8] (about=Fen, episodic, t6 @2025-02-22T10:28:00) what is the colour asking of the viewer in those prints. I think it is asking for patience rather than impact. interesting for a market setting.
[9] (about=Yuki, episodic, t14 @2025-03-22T10:17:00) My read on this is that the adjacency of Priya's architecture series and the housing documentary work creates a reading that neither has alone. The geometric and the social in tension.
[10] (about=Yuki, episodic, t4 @2025-02-15T10:09:00) My read on this is that the triangulation in the lower third of the long-exposure piece is unresolved. It is not clear whether the form is an accidental registration or a compositional choice. That ambiguity may be deliberate, but it is worth naming.
[11] (about=Bex, core, t0 @2025-02-01T10:05:00) Found a Japanese photographer's double exposure street work relevant to Sol's attempts, offers to share link.
[12] (about=Callum, episodic, t12 @2025-03-15T10:22:00) genuinely the best collaborative experience I've had, and I'm not prone to saying that. Fen kept me honest about the editorial line every time I drifted toward the interesting shot rather than the right one. lmk if anyone wants to follow the project as it develops 👍
[13] (about=Margot, said_by=Fen, profile, t6 @2025-02-22T10:04:00) Fen asks what the colour is asking of the viewer in those prints, and thinks it is asking for patience rather than impact, interesting for a market setting.
[14] (about=Nora, episodic, t6 @2025-02-22T10:18:00) That Canonet was the frame that clicked for you. I remember handing you mine for that afternoon session and you got six keepers on one roll. I knew you would buy your own the following week. 🙂
[15] (about=Priya, said_by=Otto, profile, t8 @2025-03-01T10:06:00) Otto says figural work forces a different kind of commitment from the photographer, and Priya's prints show that understanding.
[16] (about=Priya, core, t14 @2025-03-22T10:07:00) Believes the hanging layout carries as much meaning as the prints themselves, proximity between frames creates a reading not present in individual images.
[17] (about=Sol, said_by=Otto, profile, t4 @2025-02-15T10:03:00) Otto notes Sol's work requires significant contextualisation, suggesting the context is doing the work the image should do.
[18] (about=Yuki, core, t12 @2025-03-15T10:04:00) Views authorship in collaborative documentary work as about intent alignment rather than division, whether both ask the same question of the image.
[19] (about=Yuki, core, t2 @2025-02-08T10:05:00) The question is less about scanning and more about what we consider the primary object of critique.
